title: Dissipation-tunable extended and localized steady states in a non-disordered lattice
summary: Dissipation is usually regarded as a source of decoherence that suppresses quantum interference and localization. Here we show that suitably engineered dissipation can instead be used to select localized or extended states in a strictly non-disordered one-dimensional lattice. The underlying clean lattice has spatially inhomogeneous hopping and supports both extended bulk states and localized boundary states, including an algebraically localized bound state in the continuum.
